description:
Adds the `gf2-sim` tests that seeded pipelines with batch-decoding stages give identical results across worker counts, scheduling paths and decoder fallbacks.

## Background

The batch soft-decoder trait of `gf2-coding` decodes a batch of LLR frames into caller-provided decoded words and per-frame outcomes in input order. Its LDPC implementer, the LDPC batch decoder, decodes fixed waves of eight lanes with per-frame termination, routes a wave to the lane kernels or to the single-frame decoder by the decode selectors of the coding tuning section, and returns each frame's result equal to the single-frame decoder's bit for bit as `docs/reference/ldpc-decoder-numerical-contract.md` states. The CPU LDPC, 5G NR and DVB-T2 decode stages of `gf2-sim` decode their batches through it. A frame's result depends on its own LLRs alone, so no grouping of frames into waves changes it; the simulation layer adds worker scheduling and checkpointed campaigns on top, and determinism there is asserted, not inferred.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Seeded pipelines containing the CPU LDPC stage, the NR decode stage and the DVB-T2 decode stage produce byte-identical outputs for one worker, two workers and the pool default, on each scheduling path the suite exercises.
- [hard] REQ-02: The outputs are byte-identical with conservative selectors, with the lane route on the portable backend and with the lane route on the AVX2 backend.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each test meets the fast-tier budget or carries a descriptive simulation-tier ignore reason.
title: Show worker-count determinism of batch-decoding pipelines
